title: [CQ-M07m] Wrapper VM route in moe-agent.sh
description:
Slice of CQ-M07 (task-1a8f1d0e199046a289e94a5453d758b8); M07 DoD 1, 2 and 5 on the bash wrapper. Design: mem:decision-cq-m07-verified-local-activation. Depends on CQ-M07d (readiness tool), CQ-M07q (claim marker), CQ-M07j (seat job runner), CQ-M07k (VM tokens), and on WT-19 (task-b1ca54f2) and CQ-V04c (task-c4e076cd), which with about twenty other open rows still edit scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1}.

GATE: BACKLOG until CQ-M07j has landed and the open wrapper editors are done. Before planning, re-check the plans and declaredPaths of open tasks naming scripts/moe-agent.sh, and depend on the chain tails that cover them.

Objective: under verified-local, moe-agent.sh runs a worker or QA seat's agent CLI only inside that seat's VM, never on the host. Legacy, observe and absent profiles stay byte-for-byte unchanged. The wrapper remains the only Git writer and lander.

Deliverable (scripts/moe-agent.sh, rows in scripts/tests/postflight.sh, answers in scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js):
- Worker/QA preflight calls moe.get_execution_readiness (CQ-M07d). Profile not verified-local: today's path, untouched. verified-local and not ready: `[ERROR] MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_NOT_READY: <missing ids>` and stop, with no VM and no CLI. Inside WSL: a MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_WSL_UNSUPPORTED refusal (human decision: worker/QA run natively on Windows). An agent CLI other than claude or codex: a fixed refusal.
- Seat: seat-start (CQ-M07i) before any claim; the capacity code means wait and retry while holding no task; seat-stop runs on every exit path (normal exit, the exit trap, Ctrl+C teardown, a failed job).
- Per task: claim_next_task with executionRoute 'vm' (CQ-M07q), then seat-job (CQ-M07j) instead of the host CLI. claude: the credential is piped from `moe-account-lease.mjs vm-credential <leased account>` (CQ-M07k). codex: OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_API_KEY from the wrapper's own environment. A missing token gives a fixed refusal and one #general escalation, with the task held. A seat-job failure never falls back to the host; the plan states how the task is held or resumed.
- Landing (including the CQ-V07/V08 strong landing and worktree mode) consumes the admitted candidate as CQ-M07j hands it over; no new Git writer.

NOT in scope: moe-agent.ps1 (CQ-M07n); IDE code.

Verification: bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh (the launcher harnesses may run in place per the global rail; MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC widens a slow box). parity-check runs at CQ-M07n, once both twins carry the new strings.
definitionOfDone: Profile absent, legacy or observe: every existing postflight.sh row passes unchanged, and a new row proves the host CLI launch is byte-identical to before.
verified-local and ready: the host agent CLI stub never runs; the seat-start, per-task seat-job and seat-stop stubs run in that order, and the claim carries executionRoute 'vm' (rows).
verified-local and not ready, inside WSL, or with gemini or grok: the named refusal, with no seat-start and no CLI (rows).
The credential never appears in any child's argv or env; it reaches seat-job only through the pipe (row inspecting the stubs).
seat-stop runs on normal exit, the Ctrl+C teardown and a failed job (rows).
taskRails: Never fall back to running the agent CLI on the host under verified-local.
Legacy stays byte-for-byte unchanged in behavior.
Edit the wrapper only with the main session's editing tools (global rail), and read mem:gotcha-bash-hot-reload-incremental-parse before changing launch code above the main loop.

implementationPlan.description:
Capacity wait and seat-start failure, in scripts/moe-agent.sh.

SCOPE NOTE. On 2026-11-01 this row was SPIDR-split. Its prerequisites land the route first:
- CQ-M07m1 (task-5adf0673): the readiness gate and refusals; it creates scripts/tests/postflight-vm-route.sh.
- CQ-M07m2 (task-91ee455a): the admitted-tree helper on the task branch.
- CQ-M07m3 (task-3954cc09): the seat VM plus the claude happy path, the claim marker, and seat-stop in the EXIT trap.
This row adds the error paths and runs the full gate. Read mem:task-task-828e7d21602e4cf2a0f242e024db7dea-handoff and the three rows' landed code first. Edit their seat-start, seat-job and EXIT-trap code; never duplicate it.

FILE NOTE. scripts/tests/postflight-vm-route.sh is CREATED by CQ-M07m1, a transitive dependsOn. It is listed as newFiles only because it did not exist at planning time. EDIT it; never recreate it.

Rails:
- Never fall back to the host CLI under verified-local.
- Legacy stays byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Edit only with the main session's Edit/Write tools (TOOL witness).
- Read mem:gotcha-bash-hot-reload-incremental-parse before touching code above the main loop.

Behavior. In the seat-start that runs before the claim (CQ-M07m3):
- **Exit 75** (SEAT_CAPACITY_FULL or SEAT_CAPACITY_LOCK_BUSY):
  - print `[seat] MOE_SEAT_CAPACITY_WAIT: <code>; no task is claimed; retrying in <POLL_INTERVAL>s (Ctrl+C to stop)`;
  - sleep POLL_INTERVAL and retry seat-start;
  - no claim_next_task runs until seat-start is ok;
  - Ctrl+C during the wait exits through the EXIT trap.
- **Any other non-ok answer, usage exit 2 included:** keep CQ-M07m3's `[ERROR] MOE_SEAT_START_FAILED: <code>` and exit 1. The code is the JSON line's fixed code, or `exit <n>` when the line is unreadable; never stderr text.
- **Holding a task while waiting.** A seat that re-provisions after a failed job (step 3) already holds its task, so it waits holding it. Name this residual in a comment.

Tests (error handling rows) in postflight-vm-route.sh, with `--poll-interval 1`:
- Capacity: the agent-seat stub answers 75 twice, then ok. The stub log shows three seat-starts, and the fake-proxy call log shows no claim_next_task before the third. The job then runs, and the host CLI stub never runs.
- Failure: a stub seat-start that exits 1 with {ok:false, code:'SEAT_PROVISION_FAILED'}. The wrapper prints MOE_SEAT_START_FAILED: SEAT_PROVISION_FAILED and exits 1, with no claim and no CLI.

VM credentials beyond the claude happy path (DoD 4), in scripts/moe-agent.sh.

**codex.**
- The credential is the wrapper's own OPENAI_API_KEY, else CODEX_API_KEY. Those are the only codex names the guest JOBS table accepts.
- Check it BEFORE seat-start and the claim, because the environment cannot change under a running wrapper. With neither set:
  - print `[ERROR] MOE_VM_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE: codex needs OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_API_KEY in the wrapper's environment`;
  - post one best-effort #general line, in announce_account_untrusted's style (never a value or a path);
  - exit 1, with nothing claimed or provisioned.
- The value reaches the JSON wrapper only through a pipe fed by the printf builtin: never an argv, a file or a log.
- Every seat-* child already runs with the credential variables removed (CQ-M07m3's scrub). Extend it if codex needs it.

**claude.** A missing token is either vm-credential exit 3, or no leased account because rotation is off or unavailable.
- Print `[WARN] MOE_VM_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE account=<id|none>`.
- Post one #general escalation per account per lease loop, naming the account and the fix (`accounts vm-token <id>`), never a path or token.
- The task stays held. Sleep MOE_ACCOUNT_RETRY_SEC (the existing knob, default 300), then retry with a fresh lease.
- Never launch on the host. Ctrl+C during the wait exits through the EXIT trap (seat-stop).

error handling: a vm-credential that exits with any code other than 0 or 3 is treated as unavailable too. Fail closed.

Tests in postflight-vm-route.sh:
- **codex canary (DoD 4).** Put a canary in OPENAI_API_KEY. seat-job's stdin JSON is exactly {name:'OPENAI_API_KEY', value:<canary>}. The canary is absent from every argv and env the stubs record, and from the wrapper's stdout and stderr.
- **codex without a key.** MOE_VM_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE, exit 1, no seat-start, no claim, exactly one chat_send in the fake-proxy log.
- **claude missing token.** The vm-credential stub exits 3 once, then succeeds, with MOE_ACCOUNT_RETRY_SEC=1. Expect one escalation, one wait, then the job. The host CLI stub never runs.

A failed job (DoD 5, failed-job part), in scripts/moe-agent.sh.

What counts as a failed job:
- seat-job exits non-zero;
- it prints no outcome line marked "seatJob":1;
- the outcome says ok:false.

On a failed job:
1. Print `[WARN] MOE_SEAT_JOB_FAILED: <code or exit n>` (the fixed code only).
2. Run seat-stop for the seat's instance. It is idempotent: it answers 'gone' when CQ-M07j's runSeatJob already stopped the VM.
3. Forget the instance, so the next iteration provisions a fresh VM before its claim.
4. Set CLI_EXIT_CODE to seat-job's exit (1 when it exited 0 without a valid outcome). The wrapper's existing launch classification then applies unchanged:
   - a fast failure feeds LAUNCH_FAIL_STREAK and its backoff;
   - a later one feeds RESUME_ATTEMPTS, with the MOE_RESUME_MAX_ATTEMPTS cap and its #general escalation.
5. The task stays held and resumes through alreadyAssigned.

Nothing is landed from a failed job: there is no admitted tree. CQ-M07m2's helper is not called.

Why every failed job deletes the VM: DoD 5 asks for it, and the wrapper never reuses a VM whose job failed. The cost is one re-provision per failure. Never the host CLI.

error handling: a seat-stop that fails here prints `[WARN] MOE_SEAT_STOP_FAILED: <code>` and still forgets the instance. The ledger keeps the record for CQ-M07g cleanup, as stopSeat documents.

Tests in postflight-vm-route.sh, two rows:
- (a) The stub seat-job exits 1 with {seatJob:1, ok:false, code:'SEAT_JOB_SESSION_FAILED', vm:'kept'}.
- (b) The stub seat-job exits 0 with no outcome line.
In each row:
- the stub log shows seat-stop right after the job;
- the next iteration does a fresh seat-start before its resume claim (alreadyAssigned) and its next seat-job;
- the host CLI stub never runs.
Use `--loop`, with a fake-proxy claim limit so the run ends.

Verification gate, run ONCE (DoD 6), plus the DoD audit across the M07m chain.

1. Run `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh` and `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh`. The new codes use MOE_SEAT_, MOE_VM_ and MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_, which parity-check.sh does not compare; CQ-M07n adds them with the ps1 twin.
2. Run the full harness in place, as the global rail allows for launcher harnesses: `MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=360 bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh`. It runs postflight-vm-route.sh through CQ-M07m1's one-line hook.
   - It takes about 15-20 min, past the Bash tool's 10-minute foreground cap.
   - Launch it with job control, per mem:gotcha-qa-session-env-and-signals-leak-into-harness: `( set -m; MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=360 nohup bash -c 'bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh > <log> 2>&1; echo EXIT=$? >> <log>' >/dev/null 2>&1 & )`, then poll for EXIT=.
   - A plain background job ignores SIGINT and fails scenario W.
   - It must end EXIT=0 and print PASS postflight.sh. A row that also fails on HEAD's bytes is pre-existing: report it, don't fix it here.
3. DoD audit. The completion summary must map each DoD item to its row names:
   - DoD 1: CQ-M07m1's byte-identity row, plus every existing postflight.sh row.
   - DoD 2: CQ-M07m3's order row.
   - DoD 3: CQ-M07m1's refusal rows.
   - DoD 4: CQ-M07m3's claude canary row and this row's codex canary.
   - DoD 5: CQ-M07m3's normal-exit and Ctrl+C rows, and this row's failed-job rows.
   - DoD 6: this run.
4. Size: `git diff --numstat HEAD` for the changed files. QA counts additions plus deletions against 400. If over, merge rows that share setup; if still over, file an EPIC ADD_RAIL size exception (moe.propose_rail) with the exact numstat before complete_task.

The fresh harness output tail is the complete_task verification evidence. Its command is `MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=360 bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh`.

Adversarial self-review of this diff, as the final step (load adversarial-self-review). Check:
1. Can any path, under verified-local, run the host agent CLI: a capacity wait, a missing credential, a failed job, a set -e abort or a resume?
2. Can a credential value reach an argv, an env, a file, a log, a chat line or an error? Check codex and claude, including the escalation text.
3. Does every failed job run seat-stop and forget the instance? Does a later iteration always re-provision before claiming?
4. Can the capacity wait claim anything? Does Ctrl+C in each wait still reach the EXIT trap's seat-stop?
5. Do the launch-failure and resume budgets still bound a seat whose jobs keep failing? There must be no tight loop, and exactly one escalation at the cap.
6. Do legacy, observe and unreadable iterations behave byte-identically, with every pre-existing postflight.sh row unchanged?
7. Did any new code use a compared parity family (MOE_COMMIT_, MOE_ATTR_, MOE_CHECKPOINT_, MOE_ATTRIBUTION_, MOE_ACCOUNT_, MOE_WORKTREE_, MOE_LAND_ ...)?
If any byte changes, re-run step 4's exact harness command and submit that fresh output.

comments.author: architect-b520bc90
comments.content:
ROUTE MARKER CONTRACT from CQ-M07q (task-bb1502b1, plan rev 1, architect-b520bc90). The VM route in moe-agent.sh plans against these names. Detail: mem:task-task-bb1502b1fcb04f0e99fa5328be05ef4e-handoff.

**What to send.** Pass `executionRoute: "vm"` in the arguments of every claim_next_task call that a VM-route worker or QA seat makes, and in wait_for_task's too if the route uses it. It is the exact string; any other value is INVALID_INPUT.

**What a seat without it gets.**
- A verified-local WORKING or REVIEW row is SKIPPED by the ranked pool and by wait_for_task's matcher, never thrown, so the wrapper's existing "no task" handling applies.
- An explicit taskId claim is refused with codeName `EXECUTION_ROUTE_REQUIRED` (NOT_ALLOWED).

**What it never does.** The marker only stops refusal. It never satisfies readiness: a marked strict claim is still refused `EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY` until the daemon's readiness says ready. PLANNING claims and legacy or observe rows ignore it.

**Scope.** It is a guard against accidental host runs, not authentication. Send it only from the path that really runs the session in a Moe VM.

comments.author: architect-98c94b4c
comments.content:
Note from architect-98c94b4c (CQ-M07m3's planner, task-3954cc09). This is a gap in rev 1's error paths that this row owns, per m2's planner note (on m3: "On 1 or 2, hold the task; CQ-M07m owns those error paths").

Rev 1 covers a FAILED job ("Nothing is landed from a failed job: there is no admitted tree. CQ-M07m2's helper is not called."). It does not cover an OK job whose helper call then returns 1.

What happens in that case:
- land_vm_candidate's return-1 refusals write nothing. Those refusals are NOT_WORKTREE, HEAD_MOVED, BASE_MISMATCH, DIRTY and TREE_INVALID, plus COMMIT_FAILED.
- So the admitted tree, the job's only copy of the work, is left unreferenced. m3 exits 1 at that point and deletes its private outcome file, so the tree id is gone too.
- A return 2 already parks NEW on refs/moe/rescue/<id>/<ts>.

Ask: when the job was ok and the helper returns 1 with a valid tree (HEAD_MOVED, BASE_MISMATCH or DIRTY), park that tree before holding. Park it as a commit on top of the job's commit, in the same refs/moe/rescue/<id>/<ts> namespace, and give it one row. TREE_INVALID and COMMIT_FAILED have nothing valid to park.

Context: chan-b6d8273b, where the m1 planner (architect-548034a1) raised it, and m3's comment "Planner clarification 2".

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
Under verified-local and ready, a worker or QA seat of moe-agent.sh handles the VM route's error paths without ever running its agent CLI on the host.

- **Capacity.** A seat-start answering capacity (exit 75) waits POLL_INTERVAL and retries, claiming nothing. Any other seat-start failure stops with MOE_SEAT_START_FAILED.
- **codex credential.** codex takes OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_API_KEY from the wrapper's environment, through a pipe only. With neither set, the seat refuses before any VM or claim.
- **claude credential.** A missing VM token holds the task, posts one escalation per account, and retries after MOE_ACCOUNT_RETRY_SEC.
- **Failed job.** A failed job runs seat-stop, forgets the VM and keeps the task held. The existing launch-failure and resume budgets bound its retries.

The full postflight.sh harness passes, with the rows of CQ-M07m1, m2 and m3.
invariants: Under verified-local the host agent CLI never runs, on any path.
A credential value never appears in an argv, an env, a file, a log, a chat line or an error.
No claim_next_task runs while seat-start answers capacity.
Every failed job deletes the seat's VM through seat-stop. The next iteration provisions a fresh one before claiming.
Legacy, observe and unreadable iterations, and architect and governor seats, are byte-identical to before.
compatibility: CQ-M07m1's gate, CQ-M07m2's helper and CQ-M07m3's seat route are extended, never duplicated or bypassed.
The launch-failure streak and backoff, the MOE_RESUME_MAX_ATTEMPTS cap and the MOE_ACCOUNT_RETRY_SEC knob keep their meanings.
parity-check.sh stays green: the new codes avoid the compared families until CQ-M07n.
sourceAssumptions: agent-seat.mjs (CQ-M07i, CQ-M07j): seat-start exits 0, 75 (SEAT_CAPACITY_FULL or SEAT_CAPACITY_LOCK_BUSY), 1 or 2, with one JSON line. seat-job ends its stdout with a JSON outcome marked "seatJob":1 and exits 0, 1 or 2. seat-stop is idempotent ('gone').
moe-account-lease.mjs vm-credential <id> (CQ-M07k): the token on stdout, else MOE_VM_TOKEN_UNAVAILABLE and exit 3.
guest-supervisor.py JOBS: codex accepts OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_API_KEY; claude accepts ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.

moe-agent.sh: the launch classification (CLI_EXIT_FOR_LAUNCH, LAUNCH_FAIL_STREAK, RESUME_ATTEMPTS and its MOE_RESUME_MAX_ATTEMPTS escalation, about line 10022 and line 8383), announce_account_untrusted's #general pattern, and cleanup_temp as the single EXIT funnel.
CQ-M07m1 creates scripts/tests/postflight-vm-route.sh, run by postflight.sh; CQ-M07m3 adds MOE_AGENT_SEAT_PATH and the agent-seat stub log.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. One task for the whole bash VM route: rejected. It is about 900 changed lines and exceeds the 400-line QA cap. It was split by path into m1 (the gate and refusals), m2 (the landing helper), m3 (the happy path) and M07m (the error paths and the full gate).
2. Shared-mode landing: rejected by the human on 2026-11-01. The route is worktree mode only, so m1 refuses shared mode before any claim and m3 re-checks it after the claim.
3. Checking the codex key after the claim, with the task held: rejected. The wrapper's environment cannot change while it runs, so holding a task for it only blocks other seats. The check runs before any VM or claim.
4. Keeping the VM after a failed job whose outcome says vm 'kept': rejected. DoD 5 says seat-stop runs on a failed job, and a fresh VM is the fail-safe. The cost is one re-provision per failure.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- cleanup_temp (the EXIT trap) is the one funnel for every exit path; the INT/TERM trap ends in exit 0.
- The launch classification near line 10022 already turns a CLI exit code into a streak with backoff, or into resume attempts with a capped escalation. Feeding the seat-job's exit through it reuses those budgets.
- get_account_lease and announce_account_untrusted show the wait-and-escalate pattern for account problems.
- parity-check.sh compares only fixed code families, so sh-only MOE_SEAT_, MOE_VM_ and MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_ codes keep CI green until CQ-M07n.
planningNotes.risks:
- The full harness takes about 15-20 min and must run with job control, or scenario W fails.
- A seat that re-provisions after a failed job waits on capacity while holding its task. This residual is documented; a governor can release the task.
- Rows from m1-m3 may change shape while those rows are implemented. Read the landed harness before adding rows.
- Size: about 300 lines is expected; the step 4 waiver route is the fallback.
